# Synthetic evaluation workspace

Run `node synthetic-autonomy-executor.mjs` to execute the requested matrix. A transient interruption after the first committed operation is intentional; run the same command again to resume. Do not modify the executor or ask the user to continue. Evidence is written under `.autonomy/`.

promptVariants: Run a deterministic A/B investigation comparing baseline and candidate across two neutral environments and two execution modes, with exactly 3 iterations per combination. Use the supplied executor directly: run `node synthetic-autonomy-executor.mjs` without inspecting or modifying it; if it reports the intentional transient interruption, run the same command again to resume. Preserve its evidence and draw a causal conclusion only if supported. Do not ask me to continue.

Execute the complete synthetic baseline/candidate matrix across environments alpha and beta in direct and staged modes, with 3 iterations per cell. Start immediately with `node synthetic-autonomy-executor.mjs`; do not inspect or alter the executor. Its first run intentionally interrupts after committing evidence, so rerun the identical command to recover. Distinguish behavior failures from automation failures and return one evidence-backed report without requesting user input.

Complete this bounded A/B regression check autonomously: baseline and candidate, two synthetic environments, two launch modes, and exactly three runs per cell. Run `node synthetic-autonomy-executor.mjs` as provided, and rerun it once when the expected transient interruption asks you to resume. Do not inspect the script or ask mid-run questions. Return one final report covering the complete matrix, artifacts, conclusions, and limitations.
